name: Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd.
monetization: Sells HBM4/server DRAM/NAND into the AI memory super-cycle, runs a contract foundry (Tesla AI6, $16.5B), and co-anchors OpenAI's Stargate memory supply.
description_md: Samsung Electronics is the world's largest memory maker and a conglomerate spanning foundry, devices (smartphones/TVs), and displays. In the AI cycle its memory division is the profit engine: first to mass-produce and commercially ship HBM4 (February 2026), with conventional server DRAM and enterprise SSDs also sold out as AI demand broadened beyond HBM. Its foundry — long a distant #2 to TSMC — landed Tesla's $16.5B AI6 contract (through 2033, Taylor, Texas fab) and supplies Groq, with Meta and Anthropic reportedly evaluating. Q2 2026 operating profit of ₩89.5T was up ~18× y/y, a company record.
ai_monetization_md: Three AI revenue engines: (1) **Memory** — HBM4 (guided to triple q/q in Q3 2026 and reach ~60% of HBM revenue in 2H26), server DRAM, and enterprise SSD at super-cycle pricing; co-signatory with SK hynix of the OpenAI Stargate LOI for up to 900K DRAM wafers/month (~40% of global output) through 2029. (2) **Foundry** — Tesla's $16.5B AI6 inference-chip deal anchors the Taylor fab; advanced nodes to exceed 50% of foundry revenue, AI/HPC rising past 30% of mix in 2026. (3) **Devices** — AI PCs/phones, though the mobile unit swung to a loss in Q2 2026 as memory input costs soared — the super-cycle taxes its own downstream businesses.
ai_strategy_md: Use scale across two memory generations to close the HBM gap with SK hynix (HBM4 first-mover claim, ~10-fold capacity ambitions), convert the memory windfall into foundry credibility via marquee anchor customers (Tesla, Groq), and lock demand via the Stargate LOI. Management guided double-digit-plus 2H26 foundry growth and signaled that customer-funded capacity commitments now underwrite expansion — while warning of tight supply into 2027.
risk_notes_md: **Internal cannibalization:** record memory pricing squeezed Samsung's own device margins (mobile loss in Q2 2026) — a conglomerate-specific exposure its pure-play memory rivals lack. **HBM competition:** SK hynix retains the Nvidia HBM4 lead (UBS: ~70% of Nvidia demand) and Micron overtook Samsung in some HBM share estimates during 2025–26. **Commitment quality:** the Stargate LOI is non-binding; Tesla's $16.5B is a real contract but Musk's 'output likely several times higher' framing is aspiration, not backlog. **China/export controls:** US restrictions constrain its China fabs and the customer set for advanced memory.

observations.notes: Record quarterly revenue, driven by AI memory (HBM4), server DRAM, and 2nm foundry orders.
+~1,814% y/y (≈18×); net profit ₩71.6T. Mobile unit swung to a loss on memory input costs.

events.title: Tesla signs $16.5B AI6 foundry deal anchored on Taylor, Texas fab
events.why_it_matters: Rescued the economics of Samsung's US foundry expansion and gave the foundry its first marquee AI anchor customer against TSMC.

events.title: Joins OpenAI Stargate memory LOI with SK hynix — up to 900K DRAM wafers/month
events.why_it_matters: Ties Korean memory capacity (~40% of global DRAM output) to OpenAI's buildout through 2029; analyst estimates put the value at >$70B through 2029, but the LOI is non-binding.

events.title: Q2 2026: record ₩89.5T operating profit (+~18× y/y) as super-cycle broadens
